steps.title: A letter changes shape by position
body: Most Arabic letters have four shapes: on their own, at the start of a word, in the middle, and at the end. The core of the letter stays the same — only the connecting strokes change.
Take ب: on its own it is بـ at the start, ـبـ in the middle, ـب at the end. Same dot, same bowl — it just grows a joining tail.
When you write a word, you are really writing one connected shape, not separate letters with gaps.

steps.title: Six letters that never join forward
body: Six letters — ا د ذ ر ز و — connect to the letter before them but never to the letter after them. They have no start or middle shape, only on-its-own and end.
So after one of these six, the next letter starts fresh as if it were the beginning of the word. In وَلَد (walad, "boy"), the و stands alone, then لَد joins up.
Every other letter joins on both sides when it can.

steps.title: Six short words
steps.intro: Read each word, then tap 🔊 to hear it. Notice which letters join and which stand apart. Reveal the meaning to check yourself.

steps.title: Quick check
steps.prompt: Which of these letters does NOT join to the letter that follows it?
steps.explanation: د is one of the six non-connectors (ا د ذ ر ز و). ب and ن join on both sides.

steps.title: You spelled six words
steps.message: You saw how a letter changes shape by position, which six letters never join forward, and you spelled six A1 words letter by letter. Keep them in the Review view.
